sources.title: Berkowitz, Bour, Davy & Odling (2000) Scaling of fracture connectivity in geological formations. GRL 27(14), 2061-2064
sources.used_for: Connectivity framework for the topology candidate class (exponent a, fractal dimension D, density, critical length)
sources.status: Publisher abstract rechecked this session; full text read previously via a ResearchGate copy.
sources.evidence: Abstract: connectivity depends on scale of measurement for a < D+1, independent of scale for a > D+1; "Analysis of the San Andreas fault system shows that a < D+1 and that the connectivity threshold is reached only at a critical length scale." Text: a = 2.1, D = 1.65, beta = 0.0085; "connectivity is expected for L > 21 km"; "the above results are statistical, and provide connectivity estimates on averages, rather than on particular realizations". Publisher abstract states that connectivity depends on a, D and density, with scale behavior conditional on a relative to D+1; it does not validate any individual candidate gap.

sources.title: Reid, Allsop, Granser, Millett & Somerton (1990), Magnetic interpretation in three dimensions using Euler deconvolution
sources.used_for: H31-1 preregistration: structural-index-dependent Euler source solutions, depth uncertainty, window-size tradeoffs, solution clustering and geological caveats.
sources.status: Full author-hosted PDF fetched and read through page service on 2026-10-03; DOI resolves the primary article.
sources.evidence: The paper describes SI-dependent source clustering and the empirical nature of solution rejection thresholds. SI 0 approximates contacts with effectively infinite depth extent; finite/complex faults may require higher indices. Incorrect SI can bias depth. Multiple sources, poor gridding, noise and gradients can yield rejected or spurious solutions; window size trades shallow resolution against representation of deeper sources. Euler supplies source position/depth estimates, not fault dip.
